description:
Revoke one access key of a pod's port so that its value stops working. It can't be undone; a new key has a new value.
        With confirm=false (default) it only returns which key would be revoked and changes nothing; call again with confirm=true and the summary's `pod_name` after the user agreed.
        The value stops working within seconds, and so does an older value that still worked after a roll. Programs that send it then get 401. A connection that is already open, such as a WebSocket, stays open until it closes.
        Only a workspace admin or billing member can revoke keys. To replace a key's value without an outage, use roll_access_key instead.
Every write requires operation_id. Reuse the ID returned by the preview, or generate a UUID before the first call. Keep it for confirmation and all retries; a new ID means a new operation. After a timeout, check operation_status and resource state before retrying.

key_id.description: The key's `id` from the access_keys tool.
key_id.title: Key Id

pod.description: The pod_name from the pods tool. Its display name also works, except on a confirmed call (confirm=true) that opens a port, changes a key or signs out browsers: use the `pod_name` the preview returned.
pod.title: Pod

port.description: The port number, from the pod's `endpoints` in the pods tool; it must be exposed over HTTPS (`access` locked or unlocked).
port.title: Port

title: Revoke Port Access Key
